Driver Genes for Each Network Cluster

Source: R/network_diagnostics.R
plot_driver_genes.Rd

For each Leiden cluster, finds the DE genes that appear in the most GO terms of that cluster: the genes the cluster's theme is built on. Shown as a dot plot with clusters as columns and genes as rows. Dot size is the share of the cluster's terms that contain the gene; colour is the gene's log2 fold change.

Usage

plot_driver_genes(
  net_result,
  de_df = NULL,
  top_n = 5,
  title = "Driver genes per cluster"
)

Arguments

net_result

One network result from run_comparison_networks or generate_overlap_network (it must contain term_genes and go_term_df).

de_df

Optional data frame of DE results with columns gene and avg_log2FC (e.g. de_results[["Adipocytes"]]$degs), used to colour genes by fold change. If NULL, dots are grey.

top_n

Integer. Genes shown per cluster. Default 5.

title

Character plot title. Default "Driver genes per cluster".

Value

A ggplot object. Its data element holds, for every shown gene and cluster, n_terms (cluster terms containing the gene), share, and log2FC.

Details

A gene's share in cluster \(c\) is \(n_{terms}(g, c) / N_c\): the number of the cluster's GO terms whose DE genes include \(g\), divided by the number of terms in the cluster. Genes are ranked by \(n_{terms}\), with ties broken by larger \(|\log_2 FC|\), and the top top_n are shown. This measures how widely a gene is annotated across the cluster, not how specific it is to that cluster: broadly annotated genes can drive several clusters, and in a two-term cluster every shared gene has a share of 100\ range of shares shown (not 0–100\
